overview: Ethanol is manufactured primarily by fermentation of sugars followed by distillation, or synthetically by ethylene hydration. Pharmaceutical and ACS grades impose strict impurity limits (methanol, aldehydes, water).
manufacturingSummary: Fermentation → beer still → rectification → optional molecular sieve / azeotrope break for absolute ethanol. Synthetic plants use acid-catalyzed or catalytic ethylene hydration.

environmentBaseline.atmosphere: Inerting strategies for tanks and stills as required
environmentBaseline.atexZone: Zone classification mandatory for ethanol vapors

ehsHighlights: Flammable liquid — grounding, bonding, explosion protection
Methanol impurity control for human-use grades

routes.name: Fermentation + distillation (industrial)
routes.summary: Yeast fermentation of sugars to ethanol, then multi-column distillation and dehydration to target grade.

steps.title: Fermentation
steps.description: Inoculate mash or syrup medium; control temperature, pH, and contamination. Ferment to target ethanol titer.

steps.title: Distillation / rectification
steps.description: Strip and rectify ethanol to azeotrope or absolute grade using multi-column trains and optional molecular sieves.
steps.scaleNotes: Energy integration and vapor handling dominate commercial design.

scaleUp.pilotToCommercial: Column hydraulics and fire protection scale with vapor rates

sourceRefs.note: Educational industrial outline — not a plant design package

routes.name: Ethylene hydration (synthetic)
routes.summary: Catalytic or acid-catalyzed hydration of ethylene to ethanol; purify by distillation.

steps.title: Hydration
steps.description: Contact ethylene and water over catalyst or acid medium under pressure/temperature package. Separate product stream.

steps.title: Purification
steps.description: Distill and dry to grade specification.
